judge_assessment.explanation: The judge recomputed correctly and I confirm every value: C(7,3) = 35; C(9,2) = 36 with the trap 72 = 9*8 being the ordered count; (x+3)^3 = x^3+9x^2+27x+27; the x^2 coefficient of (x+4)^5 is C(5,3)*4^3 = 640; row 6 sums to 2^6 = 64; (2x-1)^4 = 16x^4-32x^3+24x^2-8x+1; the y^4 coefficient of (3+y)^6 is C(6,4)*3^2 = 135; n(n-1)/2 = 45 gives n = 10 and n = -9; the coefficient sum of (1+2x)^5 is 3^5 = 243; (a+2b)^3 = a^3+6a^2b+12ab^2+8b^3; the x^3y^2 coefficient of (2x+y)^5 is C(5,2)*2^3 = 80; and the judge's specific note is right - the signed coefficient sum of (3x-2)^4 is (3-2)^4 = 1. Standards are correctly tagged HSA-APR.C.5 from the map's binomial-theorem row. My disagreement is with instruction_following 4/4: final_response.md states 'Nothing is flagged manual' two paragraphs after describing problem 2 as 'a small find-and-fix: a classmate answers 72, and the student has to say what 72 counts'. Eight of the twelve problems print a required written slot and none is recorded.

strengths_to_preserve: All three specific-term items are built so the binomial coefficient alone is the wrong answer - (x+4)^5 needs C(5,3)*4^3 = 640, (3+y)^6 needs C(6,4)*3^2 = 135, (2x+y)^5 needs C(5,2)*2^3 = 80 - and the corresponding traps (10, 45, 20) are each declared as the expression a student produces by stopping early. Problem 11 then asks the student to say why the Pascal entry is not the answer, which is the generalisation of all three.
The directions state the point before any problem does: 'A single term needs the coefficient and both powers - the binomial coefficient by itself is almost never the answer.'

Problem 12 closes the row-structure thread honestly rather than tidily. The coefficient sum of (3x-2)^4 is (3-2)^4 = 1, and the item asks why that is so much smaller than the individual coefficients - the cancellation IS the lesson - while the trap (3+2)^4 = 625 captures the student who ignores the sign.

Pascal's triangle is printed value-free and captioned 'shown for their pattern only. No problem's numbers are taken from this display; use the values each problem gives you', removing the usual ambiguity about whether a reference figure carries givens.

workspace_cm is declared per problem (6 to 8.5 cm) so the page budget charges for the expansions the sheet actually asks to be written out, rather than treating a full expansion like a one-line answer.

root_causes.description: Every problem contains one computable number and is therefore recorded as fully machine-verified, but two thirds of the sheet also asks the student to name, state or explain something. The delivered response contradicts itself within two paragraphs - describing problem 2 as a find-and-fix and then asserting nothing is open-ended.
evidence: Problem 2 'A classmate answers 72. Say what 72 actually counts'; problem 4 'name the value of r you need first'; problem 5 'explain, using the binomial theorem, why substituting 1 for both letters in (p+q)^n gives that sum'; problem 7 'State which factor of the term the exponent on 3 comes from'; problem 8 'say which one can be a number of teams and why'; problem 9 'State the substitution that produces the sum of the coefficients of any polynomial'; problem 11 'Say why the coefficient is not simply the entry from Pascal's triangle'; problem 12 'explain what that sum tells you about the value of the polynomial at a particular input' plus 'why the answer is so much smaller than the individual coefficients'.
verify.json holds twelve entries, all typed eval/expand/series/solve; gate_log.txt step 5 reports '12 passed - 0 failed - 0 manual'.
final_response.md: 'Nothing is flagged manual and no tolerance was widened' - in the same document that calls problem 2 'a small find-and-fix'.

improvements.title: Any problem whose stem asks the student to explain, diagnose, name an error, or draw a representation must carry a manual verify entry
improvements.proposed_change: Add a rule to SKILL.md and a lint to the gate chain. Rule: a problem is machine-verified only for the quantities it computes; if its stem also carries an open-response imperative (explain, describe, justify, state why, say what/which/why, name the mistake, compare and state, plot, sketch, draw, label, complete the table) the verify JSON must carry an additional {"type": "manual"} entry under the same id describing what the written or drawn answer must contain. curr-334's verify.json in this same run is the working model - it pairs a machine entry per computed quantity with a manual entry per written diagnosis. Lint: scripts/verify.py already segments the worksheet .tex per problem for the prose-consistency gate; reuse that segmentation to scan each stem for the imperative list and fail when a matching problem has no manual entry.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture pairing curr-351's worksheet problem 4 stem ("Plot 3 + 4i. Then compute i(3+4i) ... and plot it too. Describe in one sentence what multiplying by i did to the arrow.") with a verify JSON holding only {"id": 4, "type": "eval", "expected": "-4 + 3*I"}. The lint must fail, naming problem 4 and the triggering words 'Plot' and 'Describe'. Today that exact pair builds green and reports '10 passed - 0 failed - 0 manual'.
improvements.expected_impact: Stops the delivered response claiming 'nothing on this sheet is open-ended' about sheets that are mostly open-ended, and restores the prompt's explicit requirement to label genuinely open responses for manual review. A grader currently receives a green build and no signal that half the sheet needs a human.
improvements.risk: Medium. A keyword scan over-fires on stems that say 'describe your method' as advice rather than as a graded slot, and on 'state the units' where the unit is already bound by answer_unit. Mitigate by keeping the imperative list short and explicit and by letting an author suppress a hit with an explicit "open_response": false marker on the problem, which is auditable.

improvements.title: One verify entry per printed response slot, including enumerated sub-parts and trailing second questions
improvements.proposed_change: Require the verify JSON to carry as many entries under an id as the printed problem has response slots. Sub-parts written as (a)/(b)/(c), and trailing extra questions ('Then check: what is m<A?', 'State how many zeros the theorem supplied'), each need their own entry - machine-typed where a value is computable, manual where it is not. Add a lint that, per problem segment of the worksheet .tex, counts enumerated \item sub-parts and \ansline / \answerline occurrences and fails when that count exceeds the number of verify entries sharing the id. curr-334 already satisfies this and should be cited in SKILL.md as the pattern to copy.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture from curr-301 problem 4: a stem enumerating (a) write the converse, (b) compute QR, (c) explain why PQRS makes the converse false, paired with the single verify entry {"id": 4, "type": "distance", "expected": 3}. The lint must fail with 'problem 4: 3 printed slots, 1 verify entry'. The current tree passes this fixture - it is what shipped.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the largest verification blind spot in the shard: sheets that read as fully verified while a third of what the student writes is unrecorded, and answer keys whose Quick Answers bank prints one value for a two-answer question.
improvements.risk: Low-medium. The \item count is a heuristic: a sub-part that is pure scaffolding ('redraw the two triangles separately first') is not a response slot and would false-positive. Let the author mark such an item so the exclusion is auditable rather than silent.

case_summary: A rigorous and well-varied binomial-theorem synthesis sheet. All twelve expansions, coefficients, row sums and the solve-for-n item verify independently, all eight study-guide boxes check, the seven declared traps are machine-derived from real errors, the standards tag HSA-APR.C.5 is correctly taken from the map's binomial-theorem row, and the value-free Pascal's-triangle reference and per-problem workspace_cm declarations are good print-quality practice. The defect is verification coverage of prose: eight of the twelve problems print a 'say / state / explain / name' slot, including the problem-2 find-and-fix that the delivered response itself calls a find-and-fix, and verify.json records none of them, so the build exits 0 with zero manual items and the response asserts nothing is open-ended. The mathematics fully supports the ACCEPT.
